content:
Using multiple devices on Signal at the same time? This encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to an existing Signal account, rather than limiting secondary mobile devices to iPad only.

The company also announced Android linking support today, stating: "We are expanding linked device support on iOS, allowing you to link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete message history, as well as media stored within the past 45 days.

Signal said the transfer process uses the same "link-and-sync" technology as iPad and desktop devices (including the Mac version of Signal), with end-to-end encryption throughout.

The expanded support is especially useful for users who need to keep personal and work iPhones separate, or who test multiple devices.

This move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, enabling seamless conversations between iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now rolling out on the App Store. Signal previously launched a username feature, allowing users to connect with each other without sharing phone numbers.
